_design_note: Continue the M4 opponents+BC arm for 5000 more rounds on a kill-dense table. This is the cheap form of the kill-density question and the one asked for directly: the agent already has the survival this line is best at -- pooled suicides 0.073, the lowest anything here has measured -- so the arm asks whether a skill can be added to it rather than relearned around it. Its weakness is one column: 0.148 kills against the rainbow ensemble's 0.359.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: Two, declared as two: the training table (3x rule_based -> rule_based + 2x peaceful) and the continuation seam. The control arm isolates the second.
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: The seam-control arm below, and runs/m4_oppbc_20260901 itself.
_predeclared_design_numbers.evaluation: The opponent proxy pool, both board sets, single seeds and the five-seed ensemble. The pool's mixed_weak table contains a peaceful_agent and is therefore partly familiar to the D1 arm; the verdict rests on coin3, noisyrb3, rb3 and mixed_neural.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: If the continuation on the kill-dense table is not above its own seam control, the table did nothing and what is left is the seam.
_predeclared_design_numbers.measured_kill_density: Three rule_based give 0.200 kills a round; one rule_based plus two peacefuls give 0.625. Measured over 40 rounds with the epsilon-0 weights before these arms were written (docs/05 section 0.41).
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: Kills above the source arm's 0.148 within 5000 rounds, since the policy is already competent and only the reward frequency changes. The risk is the mirror of the mixed-table failure: a policy tuned on opponents that do not compete may lose coins.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: All five training seeds, kills and suicides beside every score, the curve at rounds 1000/2500/5000 so the seam's repayment is visible, and the pool as the selection number.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reproducibility: Not bit-reproducible: rule_based_agent and peaceful_agent both seed from system entropy.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_precedent_that_argues_against_it: Two-stage fine-tuning was measured once on the M3 line and was distinguishably worse (-0.207, t = -3.77, docs/01 section 7.31). But that arm changed the SCENARIO, and its own seam control was fine (t = +0.49): the loss was the scenario, not the seam. Changing the opponent table while staying on loot-crate has never been measured.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_seam_is_a_second_factor_and_has_its_: docs/01 section 7.31.3 measured a continuation's seam -- an emptied replay buffer and a fresh Adam -- at about -0.45, repaid within 1000 to 2000 rounds. So a continuation that changes the table changes TWO things, and the control arm continues on the unchanged 3x rule_based table for exactly the same 5000 rounds. Any difference between them is the table; the difference from the source arm is the table plus the seam.
_predeclared_design_numbers.why_a_continuation: Each training seed resumes from ITS OWN round-10000 weights, not from one shared checkpoint. That matters now that the submission is an ensemble: five seeds continued from one file would be five correlated members, and the ensemble's whole gain -- +1.17 on the pool, docs/05 section 0.40 -- comes from members disagreeing. The curriculum mechanism is what warm-starts a seed from its own lineage.
_predeclared_design_numbers.why_e11: E10 anneals to a floor of 0.05 and the source arm finished there, so E11's constant 0.05 continues exactly as the first stage ended. Restarting a hold-then-anneal schedule would spend the first hundreds of rounds partly unlearning the policy.
